_comment: Ontario corporate income tax. Federal lines are composed in from t2-federal.json.

checks.message: Ontario's refundable corporate tax credits are not included.
checks.help: The innovation tax credit, the co-operative education credit and others are not computed, so a refund shown here may be understated.

checks.message: Ontario's small business limit has not been reduced, though the federal one was.
checks.help: Ontario did not parallel the federal passive income business limit reduction (2018 Ontario Fall Economic Statement), so for that reduction the full Ontario limit is right. Ontario's treatment of the federal taxable capital reduction under ITA 125(5.1)(a) has not been verified against the Taxation Act, 2007 for this build: if Ontario does parallel it, the Ontario tax shown here is understated for a corporation with taxable capital over $10 million. Have that checked before filing.

lines.label: Ontario income eligible for the small business rate
lines.note: Taxation Act, 2007 (Ontario), s. 31. Deliberately the federal limit on line 410, before the ITA 125(5.1) reductions, and not the reduced limit on line 426. Ontario declined to parallel the federal passive income reduction in its 2018 Fall Economic Statement, so a corporation with adjusted aggregate investment income over $50,000 keeps its Ontario small business deduction while losing part of the federal one. Whether Ontario parallels the federal *taxable capital* reduction has not been confirmed against the Ontario Act for this build, so neither reduction is applied here and on_t2.business_limit_not_reduced says so. Reading line 426 instead would have applied both reductions to Ontario, overstating Ontario tax for exactly the corporations this change was written for.

lines.label: Ontario income taxed at the general rate
Ontario corporate income tax
lines.note: Both rates blend, because a tax rate is in force on a day rather than fixed at a year end. Ontario's lower rate falls from 3.2% to 2.2% on 1 July 2026 and the Ontario Budget 2026 annex says the reduction is "prorated for taxation years straddling July 1, 2026". Read as `param` instead, a calendar 2026 year end would take the closing rate for all 365 days and understate the tax on the first half of the year.

lines.label: Ontario corporate income tax
lines.note: The same contract the T1 uses. It carrying over unchanged is the evidence the federal/provincial split was not shaped around personal tax.

lines.label: Ontario refundable credits
lines.note: Nil. Ontario's refundable corporate credits — the innovation and co-operative education credits among them — are not modelled, and the check says so.
